edits.text:
SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT — NONBINDING DISCUSSION DRAFT
This draft records proposals for negotiation only. Neither party shall be bound to consummate the transaction unless and until definitive documentation is agreed, approved and executed. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains unaffected.

1. Purchase Price. Seller proposes a base purchase price of USD 45,000,000 for the Shares. Buyer’s nonbinding USD 35,000,000 counterproposal, subject to Buyer approval and satisfactory diligence, is acknowledged but not accepted. The definitive agreement shall specify whether the agreed base price is expressed on an enterprise-value or equity-value basis and provide for corresponding adjustments for cash, debt, transaction expenses and closing working capital relative to an agreed normalized working-capital target, without double counting. Definitions, accounting principles, illustrative calculations, preparation and review of completion accounts, objection periods and independent expert resolution of disputed accounting items remain to be agreed.

2. Closing; Interim Covenants; Termination. The parties propose to target Closing within 30 days after execution of definitive documentation, subject to satisfactory completion of Buyer’s diligence, required corporate and regulatory approvals, required third-party consents, and satisfaction or agreed waiver of specified closing conditions. The definitive agreement shall establish an agreed diligence process and deadline and shall not provide an indefinite discretionary diligence condition. Closing conditions shall include performance of material covenants and accuracy of warranties subject to negotiated materiality standards. Between signing and Closing, Seller shall procure operation of the business in the ordinary course and compliance with agreed restrictions on material extraordinary transactions, distributions, indebtedness and disposals, subject to agreed exceptions and Buyer consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Customary closing deliverables shall include duly executed share transfers, share certificates where applicable, corporate approvals, agreed releases of security, evidence of required consents and agreed officer certificates. The definitive agreement shall include termination rights for mutual agreement, material uncured breach, a final legal prohibition and failure to close by an agreed outside date, subject to customary restrictions on termination by a party responsible for the failure.

3. Warranties; Disclosure; Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller warranties concerning ownership of and unencumbered title to the Shares, authority, capitalization, financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, litigation and compliance with law. Their scope, materiality and knowledge qualifications, applicable periods and exceptions shall be expressly agreed. Seller shall prepare disclosure schedules qualifying the warranties under agreed disclosure standards and make agreed supporting financial information available through a secure diligence process, subject to privilege, applicable law and confidentiality restrictions. The definitive agreement shall provide indemnification for agreed warranty breaches, covenant breaches and specifically identified matters, subject to negotiated survival periods, baskets, caps, claim procedures, mitigation obligations and prohibitions on double recovery. Any escrow or holdback, including its amount, duration, release mechanics and relationship to liability caps and other remedies, requires express agreement. The treatment of fraud and fundamental warranties, and the scope of any exclusive-remedy provision, remain to be negotiated.

4. Confidentiality. Subject to any existing confidentiality agreement, the definitive agreement shall require the parties to keep the transaction terms and nonpublic information received in connection with the transaction confidential and to use that information only for evaluating, financing and implementing the transaction. Permitted disclosures shall include disclosures on a need-to-know basis to professional advisers and actual or prospective financing sources subject to professional duties or confidentiality obligations appropriate to the information. Each party shall be responsible for compliance by its recipients as agreed in definitive documentation. Disclosures required by law, regulation or binding legal process shall be permitted, with advance notice where legally permissible, reasonable cooperation in seeking protective treatment and disclosure limited to what is legally required. Public announcements shall require prior agreement except where legally required.

Propose USD 35,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free enterprise-value basis, subject to Buyer approval and satisfactory diligence, with equity consideration calculated by adding eligible cash, deducting debt, debt-like items and unpaid Seller transaction expenses, and adjusting for closing working capital against an agreed normalized target. Define each category to avoid double counting. Establish completion-account procedures, accounting principles and independent expert resolution. Complete diligence before signing where practicable; otherwise agree a finite process and specific outstanding conditions. Expand warranties to address assets, intellectual property, employment, benefits, data protection, cybersecurity, insurance and environmental matters as relevant. Require specific, fairly presented disclosures rather than blanket data-room disclosure. Propose an 18-month general warranty survival period, a 15% general warranty cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and a 10% escrow for 18 months, with appropriate separate treatment of title, authority, capitalization, taxes, identified risks and fraud. Preserve the agreed interim covenants and specify the outside date, deliverables and closing conditions.
receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. The expanded framework is a constructive basis for further discussion, but Buyer does not accept the USD 45,000,000 asking price. Buyer maintains its nonbinding USD 35,000,000 proposal, subject to approval and satisfactory diligence. Please obtain Seller’s substantive response on price; Buyer is not proposing an increase at this stage.

For clarity, we propose documenting Buyer’s price on a cash-free, debt-free enterprise-value basis. Equity consideration would equal the agreed enterprise value plus eligible unrestricted cash, less debt, agreed debt-like items and unpaid Seller transaction expenses, with a dollar-for-dollar adjustment for closing working capital against an agreed normalized target. This methodology is a proposal, not an agreed interpretation of the earlier offer.

The working-capital target should reflect at least the trailing 12 months, adjusted for seasonality and substantiated nonrecurring items. Cash, debt and transaction expenses must be excluded from working capital to prevent double counting. Please provide monthly working-capital calculations and a proposed cash-to-equity bridge. We suggest estimated closing accounts before Closing, Buyer-prepared completion accounts within 60 days afterward, a 30-day Seller review period, and independent accountant determination of unresolved accounting items only. Agreed specific accounting policies should govern, followed by consistently applied historical practices to the extent compliant with the agreed accounting framework.

Our prioritized diligence requests are:
1. Three years of annual financial statements, available audit reports, current year-to-date monthly accounts, budgets and earnings-quality support.
2. Monthly working-capital schedules, receivables and payables aging, inventory detail, cash restrictions, indebtedness, security, guarantees and transaction expenses.
3. Capitalization records, ownership evidence, constitutional documents and required transaction approvals.
4. Material customer, supplier, financing and related-party contracts, including change-of-control and consent requirements.
5. Tax returns, audits and exposures; material litigation, compliance matters and contingent liabilities.
6. Material employment and benefits obligations, intellectual property, cybersecurity and privacy matters, and relevant environmental and insurance information.
7. Proposed disclosure schedules and details of any proposed pre-Closing distributions or extraordinary transactions.

Please confirm a secure data-room timetable, with appropriate handling of privileged and legally restricted information. We prefer to complete material diligence before signing. Any residual diligence condition should identify the outstanding work and a finite deadline. We support a conditional 30-day post-signing closing target, not an unconditional obligation to close within that period.

Please expand the warranty package to cover the additional diligence topics as relevant. Disclosures should fairly identify the nature and scope of exceptions; general data-room availability should not automatically qualify warranties. As an opening indemnity proposal, Buyer requests 18-month general warranty survival, a 15% general warranty cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and a 10% escrow for 18 months, retaining amounts supporting timely unresolved claims. Fundamental warranties, taxes, identified exposures and fraud require separately agreed treatment, and escrow should not be the sole source of recovery. Any exclusive-remedy provision must preserve appropriate fraud and equitable-relief exceptions.

All proposals remain nonbinding, subject to Buyer approval, diligence and execution of definitive documentation. Existing confidentiality obligations remain unaffected.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
Counsel for Buyer
